title: Quantization ↔ Precision vs Flow — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Quantization ↔ Precision vs Flow's rich face: four made pieces that put the page's questions to the ear, mistake or feel, systematic or random, to what resolution, which sounds best, and the fingerprint of the words each was made against, so the page can say when a piece may lag the text. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: "A velocity played at 73 snaps to 64 or 80, and nine levels of dynamic nuance disappear." On a grid of 16, 73 rounds to 80 (7 away; 64 is 9 away), and every velocity from 72 to 87, sixteen of them, lands on that same 80; the grid keeps 9 distinct values of 128. Suggested: "A velocity played at 73 snaps to 80, and so does every velocity from 72 to 87: sixteen levels of dynamic nuance become one." Computed by the check script, not shown by a piece; the Context names the same slip.

The 0.537 s → 0.500 s example needs its tempo back: "at 120 BPM". The nearest 16th depends on it: at 100 BPM 0.537 s snaps to 0.600 s, at 110 BPM to 0.545 s, at 140 BPM to 0.536 s. The same example sits in the opening section ("In MIDI") without a tempo too. The mistake-or-feel piece states 120 BPM; the Context records that the tempo was lost in the 2026-05-28 fold.

"With 66% swing: 0, 0.167, 0.25, 0.417". Those numbers are 2/3, triplet swing (66.7 %); 66 % gives 0, 0.165, 0.25, 0.415. The units are seconds at 120 BPM and are not stated. Suggested: "With 2/3 (triplet) swing, in seconds at 120 BPM: 0, 0.167, 0.25, 0.417". The swing-and-template piece shows all three settings side by side.

"Quantization assumes mistake" can be sharpened by what the strength knob does. At partial strength the quantizer still can't choose: it treats every deviation as the same share mistake (s) and expression (1 − s). In the mistake-or-feel piece a 37 ms stumble and a 37 ms lean keep the same share at all 101 settings; getting the stumble under 5 ms takes 87 %, where the lean keeps 13 %. Only selecting notes, a hand's act, separates them. A possible sentence: "Even at partial strength it treats every deviation alike; telling them apart is the one thing the knob can't do."

offers.section: The Final Insight: Resolution Determines Expression
offers.what: "Coarse quantization flattens reality; fine quantization preserves detail" leaves out dither, where noise buys back detail below the grid. Measured on the resolution piece's 330 Hz fade at 8 bits: undithered, the fade stops at 2.35 s and the tone holds at 0.00497 from then on; with triangular dither the tone keeps falling with the true fade (0.00188 against a true 0.00194 at 3.0 s), under a hiss. That is Advanced Applications' humanize paradox in audio: add controlled randomness and the nuance comes back. A line naming dither would link the two sections.

The in-file comment "SHOW & TELL audio examples that can have creative output, exports a sample matrix" is answered in part by the four-tracks piece: the groove is played at every part × strength, and its matrix is a timing sheet to copy. It is not audio files, because a rich-face piece's frame does not allow downloads. If that piece is approved, the comment could go, or be cut down to the part still owed (an audio export).

verdicts.why: Walks up and stays faithful, but stopSound suspends the context 250 ms later without checking play, so next-then-play (or stop-then-play) inside 250 ms goes silent (reproduced headless); fix the race, and make the stumble beat 3 "and" in both labels. The knob test is an identity by construction; the real test is whether the plants read as mistake and choice.

pieces.file: Quantization ↔ Precision vs Flow — rich — mistake or feel.html
pieces.title: mistake or feel · four steps
pieces.caption: **Ask the quantizer the section's question.** One note 37 ms late at 120 BPM, then the strength knob on that note, then a two-bar groove played freely with two plants, a kick that stumbles 37 ms late and a snare fill that leans up to 37 ms early. Last, the test: fix the stumble and keep the lean with the knob alone. No setting does; every note keeps the same share, 1 − s. Clicking notes to hold them does it at once.
pieces.near: was the deviation a mistake to correct

verdicts.why: The blind test can be decoded by a landmark: the planted stumble is 37 / 18.5 / 0 ms across the mixes and percussion separates the rest, while the hats the hint points to move only 4.9 ms RMS; play the test on a take without the plants, with hats that can be heard, say which mixes these are (0/50/100 plus the student's, not step 1's four tracks), and fix the same suspend race.

pieces.file: Quantization ↔ Precision vs Flow — rich — the four tracks.html
pieces.title: the four tracks · four steps
pieces.caption: **Part 1, done in the page.** The same freely played groove at 0, 25, 75 and 100 %; then a strength for each part (the student's kick and snare 100, hats 50, percussion 0); then the matrix of every part at every strength, with a timing sheet to copy out. Last, four mixes blind, A to D: say which grooves and which is robotic, then see which was which against the page's predictions.
pieces.near: There is no universal right answer

verdicts.file: Quantization ↔ Precision vs Flow — rich — swing and template.html
verdicts.why: Matched RMS is the right control for pattern against amount, but at 20.9 ms RMS humanize reaches 68 ms, far past the page's micro-deviations, against a template that is mostly swing (S about 0.59): say the test asks pattern against amount, not whether humanize works, and drop "the claim held"; name 66 % as the Linn/MPC label for triplet swing (exactly 2/3 at 96 PPQN); fix the suspend race.

pieces.file: Quantization ↔ Precision vs Flow — rich — swing and template.html
pieces.title: swing and template · four steps
pieces.caption: **Same amount off the grid, different pattern.** Straight 16ths, then swing as one number (the section's 66 % row, and the 2/3 it actually lists), then a groove template captured from four bars of a reference player we made and laid over a straight part. Last, blind: the template against humanize, scaled to exactly the same RMS distance from the grid (20.9 ms) and drawn fresh every pass. You say which grooves. If you pick the random one, the claim that systematic deviation makes groove did not hold for your ear.
pieces.near: Systematic deviation from grid creates groove

sections.heading: The Final Insight: Resolution Determines Expression

verdicts.file: Quantization ↔ Precision vs Flow — rich — to what resolution.html
verdicts.why: A real test with right arithmetic, but the verdict ignores dither: with dither on at 8 bits it says the fade stops at 2.35 s while the readout says it keeps falling (reproduced); and dither, a new idea, first appears on the test step. Unlock dither after both answers, or record it with each answer and word the verdict from it.

pieces.file: Quantization ↔ Precision vs Flow — rich — to what resolution.html
pieces.title: to what resolution · four steps
pieces.caption: **Two questions about one note.** A 330 Hz sine fading to 60 dB down: at 24 bits, then with bits taken away down to two levels, then the rounding error heard alone. Last, find the fewest bits at which the attack sounds clean to you, and the fewest at which the whole fade still fades. Undithered, this fade needs 12 bits to reach −60 dB. Dither, on the last step, lets 8 bits carry the fade under a hiss.
